The rule clarifies that requiring members to purchase a good, product, or service from a group will no longer automatically disqualify that group from being recognized as an association.

summary_responses.subtopic: National Park Administration, Conservation & Multi-Use Trail Regulation
summary_responses.response: The National Park Service has issued a final rule, effective December 21, 2026, allowing bicycles on about 37 miles of multi-use trails in Mammoth Cave National Park. The rule also permits horseback riding on the 5.4-mile Houchin Ferry North/Ollie Road, improving equestrian access while avoiding expected conflicts with other users. It implements the selected alternative from the park’s Comprehensive Land and River Trails Plan and Environmental Assessment, which called for expanding and reorganizing trail access. Bicycle use will shift away from the White Oak Trail and Maple Springs Connector Trail toward existing and newly constructed trails designed with sustainable techniques to protect resources. The superintendent will designate the specific trails, notify the public of where bicycles and possibly electric bicycles may be used, and manage the rule under existing National Park Service safety requirements.

key_fact_breakdown.key_fact: The National Park Service final rule for Mammoth Cave National Park is effective December 21, 2026, and allows bicycle use on approximately 37 miles of multi-use trails.
The rule allows visitors to ride horses on the 5.4-mile Houchin Ferry North/Ollie Road, expanding equestrian opportunities in the park.
Under the preferred alternative, the NPS will add approximately 66 miles of land-based trails to the park trail system, representing a 72 percent increase in trail mileage.

The rule adds eight new trails for bicycle use, including Brooks Knob Road Cemetery Trail, Brooks Knob Road Trail, Crystal Cave Road Trail, East Entrance Trail, Little Hope Cemetery Trail, Sugar Sink Connector Trail, Sugar Sink Trail, and West Entrance Trail.

In December 2024, the Regional Director for Interior Region 2, South Atlantic—Gulf, signed a Finding of No Significant Impact (FONSI) selecting the preferred alternative from the Environmental Assessment.
The final rule opens the 5.4-mile Houchin Ferry North/Ollie Road to horseback riding.
